chapter: California, Cats and the Fiddle, the Tatum trio
title: Playing with Tatum: no rehearsals, learning on the bandstand
summary: Playing with Tatum was an honor but hard; nothing was rehearsed, and riffs stayed if they fitted.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: It was an honor but it was no pleasure He made it hard. It was hard. There was never a rehearsal, not show you somethin'. or [he would] say, "no that don't go like that that go like this" or "what's the name of that chord" Whatever I learned I learned it on the bandstand. Everything, sittin' on the bandstand playing. We never had a rehearsal. And when he started playing, man, you just had to do the best you could to try to keep up. It was somethin' else. It was a hell of an experience.
Did Tatum select all the material?

We both would set riffs, and if the riff fitted and he liked it it stayed there. He wasn't a demanding guy, "You gotta do it this way, you gotta do it that way" Automatically we thought alike, if it fitted it stayed there. If he didn't play it no more then you knew it didn't belong there. So you just left it alone. That's the way that went. But if he joined in and played it with you, then that's cool.
